comparisons.peer_summary: Gamers and creators use NVIDIA GPUs for immersive experiences and content creation. The advent of generative AI is expected to drive broader adoption among PC users for local AI applications due to privacy, latency, and cost benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA identify generative AI adoption drivers, specifically highlighting privacy and latency as key benefits for local/on-device AI. AVGO describes its 'Private AI' solution as addressing privacy and compliance needs for organizations. NVDA notes that the advent of generative AI drives adoption for local AI applications because they are 'critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.' While AVGO focuses on the enterprise organizational solution for privacy, NVDA emphasizes the end-user/PC market benefits of local inference.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM emphasize privacy as a primary benefit of their respective AI strategies. AVGO's 'Private AI' solution is explicitly designed to address privacy and compliance needs for organizations. Similarly, QCOM states that generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing benefits including 'privacy, security and personalization to consumers.' Both companies frame privacy as a core value proposition of their AI offerings, though AVGO targets enterprise infrastructure and QCOM targets edge/consumer devices.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
